name: Windy & Carl
label: Kranky
lede: Windy Weber and Carl Hultgren have made slow guitar and bass drones in Dearborn since 1993, with no drummer, a mountain of delay and a record shop that kept the lights on.

eras.title: Drones, delay and a husband who teaches bass
eras.text: Carl Hultgren was already taping long instrumental guitar drones when Windy Weber joined him, learning bass from him as she went. Detroit's 1990s space-rock underground around them looked to Spacemen 3, Loop and krautrock, not the Motor City's rock heroes.

years.h: Hultgren tapes guitar drones alone, no drums, no synthesizers
years.p: Before the duo exists, he's building instrumental pieces from guitar, delay and reverb. The recipe barely changes in thirty years.
years.xp:
In the early days Hultgren wrote the music and Weber added vocals when a song wanted them. Hultgren engineered nearly every record, with one exception: Hypnos, Weber's solo experiment on a 4-track.

They record to an 8-track reel-to-reel and use a computer only to mix for mastering, so the live recordings capture the two of them playing at the same time, per Weber.

years.h: Weber's first bass song is Mudhoney's "Touch Me I'm Sick"
years.p: Hultgren teaches her the instrument, and the married pair becomes Windy & Carl in Dearborn in 1993.
years.xp:
Weber told Perfect Sound Forever the early songs had more structure than what came later, and pointed to the 7-inch tracks Dragonfly and Instrumental 1 & 2. Then the writing loosened. "We would simply sit and play, let the music pour out of us," she said.

Over time the structure melted into long tides of guitar, bass and effects, with Weber's voice low in the mix.

years.h: Blue Flea, their own label, puts out the first single
years.p: The debut 7-inch Watersong/Dragonfly is released by Weber and Hultgren themselves. Blue Flea is still issuing their records more than thirty years on.

years.h: Ba Da Bing! releases the first album, Portal
years.p: The same year, Detroit's Burnt Hair Records issues their Instrumentals EP. Burnt Hair and Zoot's Coffeehouse were the hub of the local space-rock scene.

years.h: Antarctica on Darla, Dream of Blue on Ochre, same year
years.p: Two albums on two labels, after 1996's Drawing of Sound on Icon. Weber's voice starts to surface from the haze.

years.h: A split single with Silver Apples turns into a nine-country tour
years.p: Crazy in the Sun comes out on Rocket Girl. Windy & Carl then tour with [[Silver Apples|802d971d-5fb1-4ca1-8e56-69c64122d957]] through England, France, Switzerland, Belgium, Germany, Denmark, Norway, Sweden and the Netherlands.

eras.title: The label Labradford built
eras.text: Windy & Carl wanted to be on Kranky because of Labradford, and in 1998 they got there. A record shop, a side project and a steady run of Terrastock festival sets followed, and so did a private audience with Sonic Youth.

years.big: "Labradford, who made us want to be on Kranky"
years.h: Kranky signs the Dearborn duo who came for Labradford
years.p: Depths is Windy & Carl's first Kranky album. Weber also named [[Codeine|cecd5f91-cfdd-45d1-879f-3920c7c76e58]]'s Frigid Stars as a reason they wanted the label.
years.xp: Kranky was founded in Chicago in 1993 to release [[Labradford|7cf7ef41-9637-4bf2-ae99-d8d6611ccdc6]]'s debut, and its slow, patient catalog was where Weber and Hultgren pictured themselves. Depths began a relationship with the label that ran, on and off, for more than twenty years.

years.big: "We work all day, even when we are not in the shop"
years.h: Weber and Hultgren open Stormy Records in Dearborn
years.p: The shop becomes a second career, with in-stores by [[Devendra Banhart|0110e63e-0a9b-4818-af8e-41e180c20b9a]], [[Joanna Newsom|cb69e1f1-bc76-4df5-93c9-cf97dd8a3b5c]] and [[Bonnie 'Prince' Billy|7b0a63b2-b8e8-490e-b724-1d30cb5edfe3]]. It will occupy six storefronts in 22 years.
years.xp:
Weber told Metromode in 2019 how it lasted through downloads and streaming: low personal bills, affordable leases and care with every dollar. In slow stretches, mail order kept it open. By year twenty the shop was at 13306 Michigan Avenue in east downtown Dearborn.

She recalled helping a woman find a 45 her father had recorded, and selling a six-year-old his first LP.

years.h: Five Way Mirror adds a synthesizer, and Greg Gasiorowski to play it
years.p: With Greg Gasiorowski the couple releases several singles and the full-length Transcendence. It's the rare Windy & Carl project with a synth in it.

years.h: Terrastock London hears a 28-minute piece with The Lothars
years.p: Windy & Carl release a CD with Boston's [[The Lothars|201debf5-dda7-47cd-bf44-9fce64416264]], built on that collaboration. The duo became a mainstay of Terrastock festivals, including San Francisco.

years.h: Sonic Youth gets a private show on the Consciousness tour
years.p: Windy & Carl's second Kranky album is followed by a national summer tour with Landing and a split tour CD.
years.xp: Weber told Perfect Sound Forever that Consciousness was written after her father died. Her mother's death came later and shaped the work that followed.

eras.title: After the silence, a record with a voice in it
eras.text: After a three-CD rarities box, Windy & Carl went quiet when Weber's mother died. They came back with a record dedicated to their late dog and, in 2008, the album many fans now name first.

years.h: Introspection boxes up the scattered 7-inches on three CDs
years.p: Blue Flea gathers early singles, compilation tracks and live recordings into a three-disc set.

years.h: Weber's mother dies, and Windy & Carl stop recording
years.p: According to Wikipedia and AllMusic, the band stepped away after her death while the couple kept Stormy Records running.

years.h: A record for Flea, their dog, ends the silence
years.p: The Dream House / Dedications to Flea is dedicated to the dog the couple had recently lost.
years.xp: Weber said they recorded Flea's voice, breath and footsteps as a farewell, and built instrumental pieces around them, including one dedicated to him.

years.h: Akimatsuri takes seven months to make and runs 33 minutes
years.p: One 33:16 piece in five movements, recorded from March to October 2006 and released on Blue Flea.

years.h: Windy & Carl score part of August Evening with Mono and Yellow6
years.p: The indie drama's soundtrack also features [[Mono|ffe02aed-ef7e-4736-a186-c2f1dd55ce8d]], Masakatsu Takagi and [[Yellow6|fecd919d-51c1-4451-9599-9070617ceafa]].

years.h: Weber's voice moves up front on Songs for the Broken Hearted
years.p: Ten songs on Kranky, with Weber singing more clearly than before. AllMusic says the album won Windy & Carl renewed attention, helped by praise from younger artists.

eras.title: Records when the shop allows
eras.text: Records now came when the shop allowed: an instrumental companion, a Kranky album in 2012, homemade singles on Blue Flea. Then 2020 brought a new Kranky record and Jack White's label putting their earliest demo on a Detroit history lesson.

years.h: Instrumentals for the Broken Hearted takes the vocals back out
years.p: A Blue Flea companion to Songs for the Broken Hearted, minus Weber's voice.

years.cap: Windy & Carl in a KEXP live session, Seattle, September 2012
years.h: We Will Always Be is the first Kranky album in four years
years.p: A self-titled four-song mini-album on Blue Flea arrives the same year.

years.cap: Windy Weber and Carl Hultgren live
years.h: Blues for a UFO comes out on Blue Flea
years.p: A full-length on the couple's own label, in among a string of holiday and odds-and-ends 7-inches.

years.h: Back on Kranky with six long tracks
years.p: Allegiance and Conviction, from The Stranger to Crossing Over, is their first Kranky album since 2012.

years.h: A three-CD box of 1992 to 1995 demos, each cover hand-painted
years.p: Unreleased Home Recordings 1992-1995 comes out on Blue Flea, with outtakes from their first four years.

years.h: Jack White's Third Man puts Windy & Carl on a Detroit history lesson
years.p: Southeast of Saturn compiles the city's 1990s space rock, with Windy & Carl's Instrumental #2 next to [[Majesty Crush|0cfd3007-1861-47ea-8255-9a8194af2229]], [[Füxa|0c291615-ff4a-4c55-9404-2a829484c2cc]] and [[Auburn Lull|d733cde0-4e84-4b3e-bfbd-4863939c5b7d]].

eras.title: Closing the shop, opening the amps
eras.text: After twenty-two years Stormy Records closed, and the couple finally had the time Weber had talked about for their own work. A new album and the first shows in years followed.

years.h: After 22 years, Stormy Records shuts
years.p: Weber and Hultgren close the Dearborn shop they opened in 1999.
years.xp: Weber had said in 2019 that retiring from the store would mean they could "focus even more on their own personal art and music projects."

years.h: Heavy Early & The Creation of Venus lands on Blue Flea
years.p: The newest full-length is on the label they started with their first single in 1993.

years.h: Windy & Carl play a show again in October
years.p: The duo is back on stage after a long hiatus, per setlist.fm and Wikipedia. Footage of a 2025 festival set is below.
